slides.title: Integrable Real Analytic Almost Complex Structures
slides.notes: Open by naming the modest but powerful target of the appendix. The full Newlander-Nirenberg theorem is much deeper, but this source span proves the real analytic case with tools already visible in the course: type decompositions, integrability, complexification by power series, an identity theorem, and Frobenius. Emphasize that the lecture is a proof map, not a substitute for the analytic machinery in the differentiable theorem.

slides.title: The Appendix Proves A Stronger Local Case
slides.notes: This slide isolates the theorem in lecture language. Students should hear that there are two separate upgrades: integrability removes the geometric obstruction, while real analyticity gives access to holomorphic extension. Neither ingredient alone is the whole proof. The flow diagram previews the proof order so later lemmas have a visible place in the argument.

slides.title: Almost Complex Data Splits Forms Into Types
slides.notes: Review the local linear algebra before discussing differential equations. The almost complex structure behaves like multiplication by i on tangent vectors after complexification, so covectors split into type (1,0) and type (0,1). The proof will not try to integrate arbitrary real forms; it focuses on a real analytic coframe of type (1,0).

slides.title: Integrability Removes The Barred-Barred Component
slides.notes: Connect integrability to a concrete algebraic filter. The appendix uses a formula from Chapter IX saying that torsion-free, or integrable, is equivalent to the absence of the barred-barred component in the exterior derivatives of a type (1,0) coframe. This is the exact condition needed before applying Frobenius after holomorphic extension.

slides.title: Lemma 1: Enough Type (1,0) Functions Give Charts
slides.notes: Lemma 1 is the bridge from differential forms to atlas construction. Once type (1,0) functions with independent differentials exist, they are local coordinates. On overlaps, the transition map preserves the standard complex structure because both coordinate maps respect J. A previous proposition then promotes almost complex maps between complex domains to holomorphic maps.

slides.title: The Real Work Is Integrating A Local Coframe
slides.notes: After Lemma 1, the problem has a precise local target. We already have a coframe of analytic type (1,0) forms, but coframes need not be exact. The proof must show that, after shrinking the neighborhood and changing basis by an invertible matrix of functions, the coframe comes from differentials of coordinate functions.

slides.title: Real Analyticity Opens A Holomorphic Neighborhood
slides.notes: This is where the stronger hypothesis enters decisively. Smooth functions do not automatically extend to holomorphic functions, but real analytic functions have convergent power series. The proof replaces real variables x by complex variables z and works on a small complex neighborhood, while remembering that the barred extension is a separate holomorphic object off the real slice.

slides.title: The Extended Forms Stay Independent After Shrinking
slides.notes: Independence is not a decorative condition. Frobenius needs independent forms, and Lemma 1 later needs independent differentials. The appendix uses the nonzero determinant of the real coframe and its conjugate partners, then shrinks the complex neighborhood so the holomorphic determinant stays nonzero. This is a standard but essential local compactness and continuity move.

slides.title: The Missing Component Vanishes By Analytic Continuation
slides.notes: Here the two main hypotheses meet. Integrability gives the vanishing of the barred-barred coefficient on the real neighborhood. Real analyticity turns that coefficient into a holomorphic function on U star. Since it vanishes along the real slice from which it was analytically continued, the identity theorem forces it to vanish in the complexified neighborhood.

slides.title: Holomorphic Frobenius Integrates The Pfaffian System
slides.notes: The source span does not reprove Frobenius in detail, so the lecture should clarify its role. Frobenius says the differential system is closed under exterior differentiation in precisely the way required for local first integrals or coordinates to exist. In this proof the theorem is applied in the holomorphic category, where the forms and the resulting functions are holomorphic.

slides.title: Restrict Holomorphic Functions Back To The Real Manifold
slides.notes: Do not let students lose the real manifold at the end of the holomorphic detour. Frobenius is applied in U star, but the final coordinate functions are the restrictions of those holomorphic functions to U. The equality expressing Omega in terms of dF restricts to an equality expressing omega in terms of df, preserving type and independence.

slides.title: Proof Dependency Map
slides.notes: Use this map as a mid-lecture checkpoint. The analytic hypothesis feeds the extension step, while integrability feeds the vanishing of the forbidden component. Those two strands combine before Frobenius can be invoked. Frobenius then supplies functions, and Lemma 1 converts those functions into complex charts. Each arrow is a dependency, not just a narrative transition.

slides.title: Dimension One Has No Room For The Same Obstruction
slides.notes: The source closes with the one-dimensional comparison. In real dimension two, the obstruction term has no room to appear in the same way, and the result relates to isothermal coordinates. This helps students interpret the theorem geometrically: the question is whether the local rotation field J can be straightened into the standard complex coordinate rotation.

slides.title: What The Analytic Hypothesis Buys
slides.notes: This contrast prevents a common misconception. The appendix does not prove the full differentiable Newlander-Nirenberg theorem. It proves a stronger regularity case where power series and holomorphic Frobenius can do the work. The smooth case needs analytic estimates for a nonlinear partial differential equation, which is why the main theorem is only cited in the chapter.

slides.title: Three Failure Modes To Watch
slides.notes: Use this diagnostic slide to make the proof testable. A learner should be able to point to the exact place each failure breaks the argument. Rank failure breaks Lemma 1 and Frobenius input. Torsion residual breaks integrability. Lack of analyticity breaks the passage to a holomorphic neighborhood and therefore the identity theorem step.

slides.title: Toy Lab: A Residual Parameter In A Coframe
slides.notes: This lab gives instructors an interactive thought experiment without relying on live code. The parameter c stands for the barred-barred coefficient family. When c is zero, the Pfaffian ideal generated by the Omega forms is closed in the required sense. When c is nonzero, the same formal expression shows exactly why integrability is not a cosmetic assumption.

slides.title: A Compact Teaching Script For The Proof
slides.notes: This is the board-ready version of the lecture. It is intentionally compressed so an instructor can reproduce the proof without re-reading every line of the source span. Ask students after each line which hypothesis is being used. That question reveals the architecture: analyticity is used in line three and four, while integrability is used in line two and carried into Frobenius.

slides.title: Takeaways
slides.notes: Close by returning to the geometric meaning: the almost complex structure becomes standard in suitable local coordinates. The proof is short because the analytic case lets the algebraic obstruction be moved into a holomorphic setting where Frobenius applies cleanly. Students should leave able to identify the role of Lemma 1, integrability, analyticity, the identity theorem, and Frobenius.
